photograph.author: Ianaré Sévi
photograph.description: A fiddler crab at the entrance of its burrow.
photograph.mediaType: Reference photograph/micrograph; imaging and identification require individual review
photograph.review: Actual retained reference viewed and compared with the final side/front/top, detail and action sheets on October24; source identity is not a new independent determination.
photograph.changes: Resized inside 1000 px, flattened and JPEG encoded; no generative alteration.
photograph.captionLicense: External Commons description text; retain source page and its applicable license
photograph.identityScope: Ianaré Sévi source labels a fiddler crab at a burrow under the former Uca pugilator name. A large-clawed male phenotype is selected; taxon identity, handedness frequencies and individual dimensions are not independently redetermined. Leptuca pugilator is the same retained species concept, not an extra accession.

sources.title: Pratt and McLain2002 — Antisymmetry in male fiddler crabs and the decision to feed or breed
sources.scope: Selected publisher HTML summary, methods and discussion read for Uca pugilator (current Leptuca): display major chela versus feeding minor chela, variable handedness and major-side leg asymmetry. Lateral-circular display description guides a partial authored lift, without measured path, coupled leg extension, allometric fitting, biological rate or fitness prediction.

shape.before: The earlier withheld oval/rod-limbed draft is preserved on the body sheet.
shape.changed: A distinct broader-than-long shell, narrow long eye stalks, eight banded articulated walking legs, one greatly enlarged flattened male palm and a separate small handling claw replace the symmetric generic body. The major appendage has its own whole-arm articulation.
shape.remaining: Front/orbit contours, exact claw allometry, finger dentition, leg asymmetry, joints and fine feeding setae remain unmeasured or incomplete. The major palm remains simplified. The source-labelled photo was not independently redetermined against sibling Leptuca species. Pattern/optics and waving trajectories are authored, not calibrated.

surface.changed: Muted olive/brown shell variation, darker limb bands, granular major-palm relief and narrow cream fingers replace uniform tan. The selected large-clawed male phenotype does not represent every sex or handedness.
surface.remaining: Original numerical illustration, without calibrated optics, scan or full natural variation. Front/orbit contours, exact claw allometry, finger dentition, leg asymmetry, joints and fine feeding setae remain unmeasured or incomplete. The major palm remains simplified. The source-labelled photo was not independently redetermined against sibling Leptuca species. Pattern/optics and waving trajectories are authored, not calibrated.

movement.changed: Supported lateral study, minor-claw handling, retained finger hinges, quiet support and a separate partial whole-major-arm lateral/circular lift. The display study does not reproduce the complete courtship signal or validated feeding.
movement.remaining: No measured coordinates, natural playback rate, joint limits, forces, fluid dynamics, muscle, food contact, ingestion, sensory physiology or independent biological validation. Fixed-length/support checks establish internal software consistency only.

sourceAssessment: Selected freely readable publisher sections of Pratt&McLain2002 on historical Uca pugilator, now Leptuca pugilator, were read. Major display versus minor feeding roles and coordinated wave context are distinguished. Ianare Sevi's CC BY-SA3.0 photograph was compared. No measured wave rate, coupled major-side leg extension, mate response or force was imported.
fixesAfterRenderedReview: Flattened the major palm and turned it to expose its side instead of a round end-on mass.
Reduced coarse pale shell mottling, thick fingers and oversized triangular cutting teeth after the enlarged comparison sheet.
Raised the folded major arm in quiet support after the floor-clearance check caught an intersection; all57 affected comparison states replaced.

assessmentRubric.identity: Accepted species-rank concept checked; photographed organism remains source-labelled
assessmentRubric.body: Substantial initial correction; unmeasured dimensions and incomplete fine diagnostic anatomy
assessmentRubric.texture: Distinct selected numerical surface; optics and microanatomy remain illustrative
assessmentRubric.movement: Working qualitative supported articulation; empirical rate/dynamics unvalidated

reviewMethod: 57 actual final nonblank side/front/top, enlarged and action/posture states inspected individually on labelled sheets against the authentic photograph and scoped sources. Superseded frames excluded. Qualitative author assessment, not independent expert certification.

samples.status: Actual final frame visually inspected on labelled comparison sheets; qualitative author assessment
samples.finding: A distinct broader-than-long shell, narrow long eye stalks, eight banded articulated walking legs, one greatly enlarged flattened male palm and a separate small handling claw replace the symmetric generic body. The major appendage has its own whole-arm articulation. Muted olive/brown shell variation, darker limb bands, granular major-palm relief and narrow cream fingers replace uniform tan. The selected large-clawed male phenotype does not represent every sex or handedness. Remaining: Front/orbit contours, exact claw allometry, finger dentition, leg asymmetry, joints and fine feeding setae remain unmeasured or incomplete. The major palm remains simplified. The source-labelled photo was not independently redetermined against sibling Leptuca species. Pattern/optics and waving trajectories are authored, not calibrated.
